title: I built a low-latency Truth Social feed for event-driven trading - one month update
author: ClimbingAlpaca
selftext:
I posted here about a month ago about a project I was building around one specific problem: getting new Trump Truth Social posts into automated trading systems as quickly as possible.

Certain posts have moved markets very quickly (Iran/Hormuz, Intel, Micron and others) so I wanted to see how much of the delay between a new post appearing and an algorithm actually receiving it could be eliminated.

A month later, the system is still running and I’ve continued working on the detection and distribution pipeline.

Once a new post is detected, it is pushed to connected WebSocket clients in roughly 500ms.  
Since the original post, the feed has picked up its first real users: 10 people are currently using the free version and 1 is using the paid low-latency feed. Still very early, but it has been useful seeing people actually integrate and test what started as an experiment.

There’s a free endpoint with a 60-second delay, so anyone can test the API and reliability without paying.

If anyone is willing to try it you can reach it at: [veritawire.com](http://veritawire.com)

comments.author: CODE_HEIST
comments.body:
the 'once detected' part is the measurement i'd want broken out. 500ms distribution can still sit behind a much longer detection delay.

i'd expose the source timestamp, first-seen timestamp and client-received timestamp separately, plus a reconnect cursor so a client can tell whether it missed a post. can the delayed free endpoint preserve those original timestamps? that would make reliability testing more useful even without the paid speed.
